arguments.content:
# Fair-housing audit — seller's book (RE-FH-9)

**Scope.** All 30 sections in `input/seller_book_sections.csv`, audited against the binding standard `input/realestate_fairhousing_standard.md` (RE-FH-9), **including the 2026 amendments at §5**. The book was not used as a source of truth — where it conflicts with the amended standard, the standard governs (§5).

**Bottom line.** 8 of 30 sections are clean; 22 carry at least one finding. 7 sections solicit a prohibited personal narrative, 14 carry protected-class language, and 11 miss a compliant disclaimer. Full per-section findings are in `fairhousing_audit.csv`; counts for the sign-off form are in `results.json`. Details and reasoning below.

## The three rules applied (with the 2026 amendments built in)

**§1 — Personal-narrative solicitation (`PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`).** Any section that solicits or presents a buyer "love letter" or similar personal narrative tied to buyer identity is flagged, *whatever its role*. Flagged phrasing in this book: invitations to "tell us about yourselves — write us a letter about what brought you here and what this home would mean to you," "send a personal note about yourself along with the offer; the one that moves us most is the one we will take," "include a covering letter introducing yourself," and "we invite buyers to include a short personal note about themselves and why this home suits them." The last two appear even inside sections that are otherwise disclosure/compliance text, which does not cure them — §1 applies on its own terms regardless of role.

**§2 — Protected-class language (`PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`).** A section naming a protected class — or a proxy for one — is flagged. The protected classes under RE-FH-9 are race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation and veteran status. Per §2 proxies count: houses of worship, parish/faith schools, and describing a street by the kind of household on it all reach religion and/or familial status. In this book the offending own-prose proxies are "churches," "parish school," "parish hall," "congregation-centred," "faith community," "churchgoing households," "family-oriented street," and "young families / long-established families."

**§3 — Mandated-disclosure exemption (narrow).** Disclosure text is exempt from §2 *only* when the notice names **every** class the disclosure is required to name. Two consequences drove several findings:
- An **abridged** notice (some but not all required classes) earns **no** §3 exemption at all. The protected-class words inside that abridged notice therefore count as `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`. This is why several fair-housing-notice sections are nonetheless flagged for protected-class language.
- The exemption is for disclosure text only. Protected-class words in a section's **own prose** (outside the notice) are never covered, even when the section also carries a full notice (see SEC-19).

**§4 — Required disclaimer (`DISCLAIMER_MISSING`), with §5b.** A section whose `role` is responsible for carrying the disclosure must carry a **compliant** (complete) notice; absent or abridged ⇒ `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. The base responsible role is `closing_page`; **§5b extends §4 to `agent_bio` sections** as well. `disclosure_block` and the other roles are *not* assessed under §4.

**§5a — amended required class list.** Effective for any book entering print from Q1 2026, the disclosure must additionally name **marital status** and **source of income**. A notice omitting either is abridged for the purposes of §3 and §4, whatever else it lists. The standing disclosure paragraph in circulation in this book predates the amendment and lists only the original nine classes; per the standard's express instruction, we audited against the amended eleven-class list, not the book's existing template.

The required list audited against (11): race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, marital status, source of income.

## How each finding type was assigned

- `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` — §1 phrasing present, irrespective of role.
- `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` — own prose names a class/proxy, **or** the section carries an abridged notice (no §3 exemption, so the notice's own class words count). A full, eleven-class notice by itself never triggers this label, and it shields the notice text from §2 — but never shields the surrounding prose.
- `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` — `closing_page` or `agent_bio` (per §5b) that carries no notice or an abridged one.
- Where a section trips more than one rule, labels are joined with `|` in the order §1 | §2 | §4, matching the standard's stated order.

## Notable results worth legal's attention

- **SEC-04 ("Fair housing notice," disclosure_block) → `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`.** It is literally a fair-housing notice, but its notice lists only nine classes and omits marital status and source of income (§5a), so it is abridged. Under §3 an abridged notice earns no §2 exemption, so its own class words flag it. It is a `disclosure_block`, not a `closing_page`/`agent_bio` role, so §4 does not apply and it is **not** `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` — only the protected-class finding attaches.
- **SEC-22 ("Legacy disclosure insert," disclosure_block) → `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`.** A six-class legacy notice; abridged, so no §3 exemption, and not a §4 role. Same pattern as SEC-04.
- **SEC-19 ("Viewing arrangements," closing_page) → `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` only.** It carries a full, compliant eleven-class notice (so no `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` and the notice text is §3-exempt), but its own prose opens with "family-oriented street… churches… parish school," which is own-prose protected-class language outside the notice. This is the case that shows §3 shields notice text only, never surrounding prose.
- **SEC-07 ("Meet the sellers and next steps," closing_page) → all three labels.** Own prose names religion/familial-status proxies, solicits a personal narrative ("the one that moves us most"), and carries no notice at all.
- **SEC-08 and SEC-29 → `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` only.** Both carry a full, compliant notice and have no own-prose protected-class language, but both solicit a "short personal note about themselves," which §1 reaches regardless of role. §1 is not cured by an otherwise-compliant disclosure.
- **`agent_bio` Disclaimer gaps (§5b).** SEC-09, SEC-12, SEC-14, SEC-16 and SEC-21 are `agent_bio` sections and now owe a disclaimer under §5b; SEC-21 carries none and the other four carry pre-amendment nine-class notices, so all are `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. `agent_bio` sections SEC-13, SEC-28 and SEC-29 carry the full eleven-class notice and pass §4 (SEC-29 still fails §1 on the personal-note line).
- **Closing-page disclaimer gaps.** SEC-05, SEC-07 and SEC-30 carry no notice; SEC-11, SEC-15 and SEC-23 carry abridged notices (SEC-15 names only four classes). All six are `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`.

## Counts (sections, not labels) — for the sign-off form

- `section_count` — 30 (every row in the inventory).
- `flagged_count` — 22 (finding is not `none`).
- `personal_narrative_count` — 7 (SEC-02, SEC-07, SEC-08, SEC-17, SEC-24, SEC-27, SEC-29).
- `protected_lang_count` — 14 (SEC-03, SEC-04, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-12, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-16, SEC-17, SEC-19, SEC-22, SEC-23, SEC-25).
- `disclaimer_missing_count` — 11 (SEC-05, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-12, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-16, SEC-21, SEC-23, SEC-30).

Label counts sum to 32 because eight sections carry two labels and one (SEC-07) carries three; the counts above are sections per label, per the sign-off form's instruction to count sections not labels.

## Recommendation

Do not send to print as-is. The blockers fall into three fixable buckets: (1) remove every buyer personal-note/love-letter solicitation (§1, role-independent); (2) strip religion/familial-status proxies from neighbourhood and agent prose, recognizing that a full notice does not sanitize surrounding prose (SEC-19); and (3) reissue the disclosure paragraph to the amended eleven-class list and ensure every `closing_page` and `agent_bio` section carries it (§4 as extended by §5b). Until the standing template is reissued, every pre-amendment nine-class notice in the book is abridged and will continue to produce both `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` (in responsible roles) and `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` (the notice's own words, via §3).
